To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antibacterial potency of BPI, a potent antibacterial protein isolated from rabbit PMNs, can be enhanced up to 50 times in the presence of sublethal amounts of p15A and NP-1.

(a) the antibacterial action of BPI is enhanced synergistically by the cationic defensin NP -1, and that (b) this action is also enhanced by the 15-kD cationic protein p15A, but not by other defensin species.

BPI, p15A, and NP-1, three proteins of rabbit granulocytes, have distinct antibacterial activities against E. coli, and that the combination of BPI and either p15A or the defensin NP -1 is more potent than any of the three proteins alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, purification, and characterization of the most potent antimicrobial proteins of rabbit polymorphuclear leukocytes (PMNs) and their combined action.
the antibacterial properties of the major proteins in rabbit granulocyte acid extracts.
the characterization and mechanism of action of the antibacterial proteins BPI, p15, and defensin NP -1.
